name: L1_3 medium Copper Pourbaix diagram with ammonia complexes

content.text: Build a 2-D Pourbaix diagram for copper in 0.1 M total ammonia, with 1 mM Cu, at 25 C and I=0.1 m. Prefer hydroxide solids. Identify the E-pH window where soluble Cu-ammine complexes dominate over Cu(OH)2(s) and metallic Cu.

Gathering thermodynamic data for copper-ammonia species.
Correcting activity coefficients for ionic strength effects.
Working out formation constants for hydroxide species.
Setting up equilibrium constants for copper and ammonia species.
Determining solid-versus-dissolved dominance across the pH-potential grid.
Applying Davies corrections to copper-ammine equilibrium constants.

mkdir -p /home/claude && cat > /home/claude/pourbaix.py << 'EOF'
import numpy as np, matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.colors import ListedColormap

# ---------------- conditions ----------------
T=298.15; F=96485.; R=8.314; s=2.302585*R*T/F   # 0.05916 V/decade
I=0.1; CuT=1e-3; NT=0.1
def lg(z): return -0.509*z*z*(np.sqrt(I)/(1+np.sqrt(I))-0.3*I)   # Davies
g1,g2=lg(1),lg(2)

# ---------------- constants (concentration basis at I=0.1, H+ as activity) ----------------
pKa_NH4 = 9.29                       # Smith & Martell, 0.1 M
logb2 = [4.13, 7.61, 10.48, 12.59]   # Cu(NH3)n2+, n=1..4, 0.1 M
logb1 = [5.93, 10.86]                # Cu(NH3)n+,  n=1,2 (lit. values, higher I; caveat)
# hydroxo (IUPAC/Powell 2007, I=0 -> Davies to I=0.1); *beta_n : Cu2+ + nH2O = Cu(OH)n + nH+
logOH = {1:-7.95-(g1-g2), 2:-16.2-(0-g2), 3:-26.6-(-g1-g2), 4:-39.7-(g2-g2)}
logK_CuI   = 0.153/s -(g1-g2)        # Cu2+ + e = Cu+
logK_Cu0   = 2*0.340/s -(0-g2)       # Cu2+ + 2e = Cu(s)
logKs_CuOH2= -8.64 -(0-g2)           # Cu2+ + 2H2O = Cu(OH)2(s) + 2H+  (log*Ks0 = 8.64, fresh)
logK_Cu2O  = 2*0.203/s -(0-2*g2)     # 2Cu2+ + H2O + 2e = Cu2O(s) + 2H+

# ---------------- grid ----------------
pH=np.linspace(0,14,701); E=np.linspace(-1.0,1.5,626)
PH,EE=np.meshgrid(pH,E); pe=EE/s

names=["Cu2+","CuOH+","Cu(OH)2(aq)","Cu(OH)3-","Cu(OH)4 2-",
       "Cu(NH3)2+","Cu(NH3)2 2+","Cu(NH3)3 2+","Cu(NH3)4 2+",
       "Cu+","Cu(NH3)+","Cu(NH3)2+ (I)"]
nNH3=np.array([0,0,0,0,0,1,2,3,4,0,1,2])

def speciation(nh3):
    # factors f_i = c_i/[Cu2+]
    f=[np.ones_like(PH)]
    for n in (1,2,3,4): f.append(10**(logOH[n]+n*PH))
    for n,b in enumerate(logb2,1): f.append(10**b*nh3**n)
    cuI=10**(logK_CuI-pe); f.append(cuI)
    for n,b in enumerate(logb1,1): f.append(cuI*10**b*nh3**n)
    return np.array(f)

nh3=NT/(1+10**(pKa_NH4-PH))
for it in range(60):
    f=speciation(nh3); S=f.sum(0)
    cu_unsat=CuT/S
    cu_Cu0 =10**(-logK_Cu0+2*pe)
    cu_Cu2O=10**(-PH-0.5*logK_Cu2O+pe)
    cu_CuOH2=10**(-logKs_CuOH2-2*PH)
    cu=np.minimum.reduce([cu_unsat,cu_Cu0,cu_Cu2O,cu_CuOH2])
    conc=f*cu; bound=(nNH3[:,None,None]*conc).sum(0)
    nh3_new=(NT-bound)/(1+10**(pKa_NH4-PH))
    nh3=0.5*nh3+0.5*nh3_new

# ---------------- dominance ----------------
solid=np.argmin(np.array([cu_unsat,cu_Cu0,cu_Cu2O,cu_CuOH2]),0)  # 0 aqueous
aq=np.argmax(conc,0)
dom=np.where(solid==0,aq,11+solid)   # 12 Cu(s),13 Cu2O,14 Cu(OH)2
labels=names+["Cu(s)","Cu2O(s)","Cu(OH)2(s)"]

# ---------------- plot ----------------
cols=["#f4c2c2","#f9d9b0","#fbe7a1","#e6f0a3","#c9e6a3",
      "#a3d5f0","#8fc6ea","#7bb7e3","#5fa4d8",
      "#e0c3f0","#c9a5e6","#b48ad9",
      "#b0b0b0","#c8a27a","#7fbf9a"]
fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(9,7.5))
ax.pcolormesh(PH,EE,dom,cmap=ListedColormap(cols),vmin=-0.5,vmax=14.5,shading="auto")
ax.contour(PH,EE,dom,levels=np.arange(-0.5,15,1),colors="k",linewidths=0.6)
ax.plot(pH,1.229-s*pH,"k--",lw=1); ax.plot(pH,-s*pH,"k--",lw=1)
ax.text(0.3,1.30,"O$_2$/H$_2$O",fontsize=8); ax.text(0.3,-0.12,"H$_2$/H$^+$",fontsize=8)
ax.text(0.8,-0.6,"Cu(s)",fontsize=12,weight="bold")
# label regions at centroid
pretty={"Cu2+":"Cu$^{2+}$","CuOH+":"CuOH$^+$","Cu(OH)2(aq)":"Cu(OH)$_2$(aq)","Cu(OH)3-":"Cu(OH)$_3^-$",
 "Cu(OH)4 2-":"Cu(OH)$_4^{2-}$","Cu(NH3)2+":"Cu(NH$_3$)$^{2+}$","Cu(NH3)2 2+":"Cu(NH$_3$)$_2^{2+}$",
 "Cu(NH3)3 2+":"Cu(NH$_3$)$_3^{2+}$","Cu(NH3)4 2+":"Cu(NH$_3$)$_4^{2+}$","Cu+":"Cu$^+$",
 "Cu(NH3)+":"Cu(NH$_3$)$^+$","Cu(NH3)2+ (I)":"Cu(NH$_3$)$_2^+$","Cu(s)":"Cu(s)","Cu2O(s)":"Cu$_2$O(s)","Cu(OH)2(s)":"Cu(OH)$_2$(s)"}
for k,l in enumerate(labels):
    m=dom==k
    if m.sum()<150: continue
    x=PH[m].mean(); y=EE[m].mean()
    if l=="Cu(s)": continue
    ax.text(x,y,pretty[l],ha="center",va="center",fontsize=9,
            bbox=dict(fc="white",alpha=0.6,ec="none",pad=1))
ax.set_xlabel("pH"); ax.set_ylabel("E / V vs SHE")
ax.set_title("Cu Pourbaix diagram, 25 °C, I = 0.1 m\n[Cu]$_T$ = 1 mM, [NH$_3$]$_T$ = 0.1 M, Cu(OH)$_2$(s) as Cu(II) solid")
ax.set_xlim(0,14); ax.set_ylim(-1,1.5)
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig("/mnt/user-data/outputs/Cu_NH3_pourbaix.png",dpi=160)

# ---------------- ammine window ----------------
amm=np.isin(dom,[5,6,7,8,10,11])
print("Ammine-dominated pH range: %.2f - %.2f"%(PH[amm].min(),PH[amm].max()))
for p in [6,7,8,9,9.3,10,11,12]:
    j=np.argmin(abs(pH-p)); col=amm[:,j]
    if col.any():
        Es=EE[col,j]; dj=dom[col,j]
        print("pH %4.1f: E = %+.3f to %+.3f V ; species: %s"%(p,Es.min(),Es.max(),
              ", ".join(labels[k] for k in np.unique(dj))))
    else: print("pH %4.1f: no ammine region"%p)
# widest window
w=np.array([ (EE[amm[:,j],j].max()-EE[amm[:,j],j].min()) if amm[:,j].any() else 0 for j in range(len(pH))])
j=w.argmax(); print("Widest window at pH %.2f: E %+.3f to %+.3f V"%(pH[j],EE[amm[:,j],j].min(),EE[amm[:,j],j].max()))
# Cu(I) vs Cu(II) ammine split at pH 9.3
j=np.argmin(abs(pH-9.3))
for k in [10,11,8]:
    m=dom[:,j]==k
    if m.any(): print("  pH 9.3 %s: E %+.3f to %+.3f"%(labels[k],EE[m,j].min(),EE[m,j].max()))
EOF

content.text: Good. Copying the script alongside the figure so the constants can be swapped.
The file cards appear at the end of your reply if it ends with text, otherwise under this step; say they are below only if you finish the reply with text.

**Ammine window (soluble Cu–NH₃ complexes predominate, no Cu(s) or Cu(OH)₂(s)):**

- **pH ≈ 8.2 – 10.2 (Cu(II)):** Cu(NH₃)₄²⁺ is the predominant species from E ≈ +0.19 V (SHE) up through the O₂ line. Above pH ~10.2, Cu(OH)₂(s) wins because free NH₃ stops increasing (NH₄⁺/NH₃ pKa ≈ 9.3) while [OH⁻] keeps climbing; below ~8.2, free NH₃ is too low to hold 1 mM Cu in solution against Cu(OH)₂ precipitation.
- **pH ≈ 7.5 – 11.1 (Cu(I)):** a Cu(NH₃)₂⁺ band sits between the Cu(s) floor and the Cu(II) region. At pH 9.3 it spans about −0.14 V to +0.18 V; at pH 10 about −0.17 V to +0.20 V.
- **Widest all-soluble window:** at pH ~10, E from ≈ −0.17 V (Cu(s) deposition) to ≈ +1.5 V, with the Cu(I)/Cu(II) ammine handoff at ≈ +0.20 V. Outside 8.2–10.2, only the low-E Cu(I) ammine band survives, capped by Cu(OH)₂(s) or Cu₂O(s).

Practical reading: to keep copper dissolved as ammine, hold pH ≈ 9–10 and E > −0.15 V; anything more reducing plates Cu(s).

**Model notes:** grid calculation, 1 mM Cu_T and 0.1 M NH₃_T mass balances solved at every (E, pH); solid drawn where the solution is saturated. Constants: Cu(NH₃)ₙ²⁺ log β = 4.13/7.61/10.48/12.59 and pKa(NH₄⁺) = 9.29 (0.1 M, Smith–Martell); Cu(NH₃)ₙ⁺ log β = 5.93/10.86 (literature values at higher ionic strength, the main uncertainty in the Cu(I) band); hydroxo complexes from IUPAC (Powell 2007) with Davies correction to I = 0.1; Cu(OH)₂(s) log *Ks0 = 8.64 (fresh precipitate, per your hydroxide preference, rather than tenorite, which would shrink the ammine windows by roughly a pH unit each side). No well-defined CuOH(s) exists, so Cu₂O is the Cu(I) solid. Cu₂(OH)₂²⁺ was omitted (negligible at 1 mM). Thin Cu(NH₃)²⁺ and Cu(NH₃)₃²⁺ slivers appear at the Cu(OH)₂ edges (arrowed). The script is attached if you want to swap in aged Cu(OH)₂, tenorite, or different ammine constants.
